intro: Which claims a Verifiable Credential issued by this service carries, from now on. Nothing already issued changes — a credential is a signed document and this page cannot reach inside one. It applies to all five OID4VCI configurations: the SD-JWT VC, the jwt_vc_json W3C credential, the ldp_vc one with a BBS proof, and the two whose only difference is that the issuer names itself by DID.
ldapTypes: The list is of LDAP attribute types and not of claim names, because this service has a directory and a claim with a value nothing else can see is half a demonstration. A selected attribute becomes the claim named beside it, and the value is the one on that person's entry under ou=users — so an LDAP client and an OID4VCI wallet pointed at this service are shown the same person. Three rows are not RFC 4519/4524/2798: there is no standard attribute type for a birthdate or a nationality, so the SCHAC schema's names are borrowed rather than invented.
garbage: None of this is verified, and the values are garbage on purpose. This service authenticates nobody — the username typed at the sign-in screen is the identity in every token and credential it issues — so there is no source of a real birthdate here and there had better not be. What a person is missing is invented from their username: the same invented person every time, across restarts, so that two credentials issued a minute apart describe one human being rather than two. A verifier that believed any of it would be believing this page.
sources1: Three sources, in this order. The access token, where it carries a claim of that name — that is a statement this service already made about the person, from the sign-in or from the
sources2: page, and a credential contradicting the token that authorised it would be indefensible. Then the directory entry, which is where the generated values live once an entry exists and also where an ldapmodify lands: change mail on uid=alice,ou=users and the next credential says so. Then the generated persona, for a person with no entry, or an entry without that attribute, or a directory that is not running.
neverOverwrites: Populating never overwrites. An attribute an entry already carries is left exactly as it is — which is why the three seeded people keep their names and only gain what they had nothing for, and why a sweep run twice does nothing the second time.
hNotDo: What these claims do not do
notDo1: Nothing reads them back. No access token, ID Token, SAML assertion or Kerberos PAC carries a claim from this page, and no endpoint makes a decision on one — it reaches a credential and stops there. The
notDo2: page shows the directory entry each of these values was written onto.
saveNote: Saving also populates the directory: every person under ou=users gains the attributes they are missing.
entryFound: This person has an entry in the directory, so the values below marked directory are what an LDAP client reads from it.
entryMissing: This person has no entry in the directory — nobody has authenticated as them and nothing was added by hand — so every value below is generated. It will be the same one next time: the invented person is seeded from the username.
noneSelected: No attribute is selected, so a credential carries nothing but its subject identifier. That is a legitimate thing to test and is not a mistake this page will correct.
ldpOmitted: {n, plural, one {is selected and does} other {are selected and do}} not appear in an ldp_vc credential. That format is signed over canonicalized JSON-LD, so it can only carry terms the vendored context defines, and the context is vendored precisely because editing it would invalidate every credential already issued against it. The two JOSE-secured formats carry all of them.
